overview: This event pulls together pel profile and procedures, plus any ep into a cumulative review brief. You should be ready to move between sections without a reset and explain the setup cues, decision points, and common misses that usually trigger follow-up questions.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

children.text: Turn, Climb, Clean, Check, BIP, Determine, Deliver, Reduce, Lower, Report
Clean configuration (gear, flaps, speed brake up)
Boost pump and Ignition - as required (ON unless airstart not warranted)
Climb or accelerate to intercept DEGA (140 KIAS climb or increase airspeed if unable to climb)
Execute PEL at or above 400’ AGL
Review the associated WARNINGs, CAUTIONs, and NOTEs for PEL Profile and Procedures before the event.

items.text: Treat this as a cumulative EP brief. The instructor can move quickly between recognition, memory items, and the branch logic that decides whether you continue, land, or eject.

children.text: Emergency Engine Shutdown on the Ground
Be able to state the recognition cue before you recite the steps.
Know the associated N/W/Cs, not just the memory items.
Have a clear answer for when the EP becomes a PEL, forced-landing, or ejection problem.

studyNotes.summary: Keep PEL Profile and Procedures, plus Any EP organized early, then know the immediate actions, branch logic, and N/W/C details before you start improvising.
